issues.detail: The Greek 'ο δε μετα ορκωμοσιας' (but he who is after an oath) refers to the person/subject of the oath. The Vietnamese 'được lập lên bằng lời thề' (was appointed by an oath) changes the grammatical structure from a description of the subject to a passive action performed on the subject.
The Greek 'συ ιερευς' (as a priest) is rendered as 'Con làm thầy tế lễ' (I am/become a priest). The Vietnamese adds the first-person pronoun 'Con' (I/Me), which is not present in the Greek text.
